tasks.title: History harvest and grader engine for artifact-grounding-judge
tasks.description: Build the zero-token history path end to end for one agent. A new script claude-code-shared/scripts/agent-eval/harvest.py takes an agent name, scans ~/.cch/projects and ~/.cco/projects for subagents/agent-*.jsonl files whose spawn matches that agent, and writes one history record per spawn (spawn prompt from the first user line, final output text, tool calls with arguments, files written, token usage, timestamp, session id) to a gitignored cache under .claude/agent-bench/<agent>/history/. A new claude-code-shared/scripts/agent-eval/grade.py reads a contract.json plus records and prints per-check pass/fail and pass rate. It implements exactly the 7 built-in check types from the seed: json_parse, schema, quote_in_input, tool_called, file_written, verdict_equals, no_prose. Grading is deterministic. No LLM is called. Per-agent data (contract.json, cases.jsonl, lock file, gitignored fixtures/) lives in claude-code-shared/evals/<agent>/. Run results, traces, history and queue live under .claude/agent-bench/. Add .gitignore and repo-policy excludes so fixtures/, traces/ and history/ are never committed.
acceptance_criteria: harvest.py artifact-grounding-judge writes history records for its recorded spawns across both config dirs and prints the count found
grade.py runs a hand-written sample contract (format check plus tool_called log-learning.py) over those records and prints per-check pass rates without calling any model

No unit test files (per the no-unit-tests-for-infra rule). Verified by running both scripts on real artifact-grounding-judge history and spot-checking 3 records against their source agent-*.jsonl by hand
git status shows no fixtures/, traces/ or history/ paths as committable after a run
tasks.summary: Added harvest.py and grade.py under scripts/agent-eval/ (7 deterministic check types), sample contract, gitignore and repo-policy excludes. 21 spawns found for artifact-grounding-judge (seed expected about 300).

tasks.title: Skill skeleton and contract stage with cited sources and history-validated approval
tasks.description: Create claude-code-shared/skills/improve-agent-benchmarks/SKILL.md. /improve-agent-benchmarks <agent> targets that agent. With no name, the first step asks which agent (a simple list of agents for now; ranking comes in a later task). The skill reads .claude/agent-bench/queue.json, creates the agent's entry at stage contract if missing, and runs the contract stage. Contract stage: an Opus subagent drafts contract.json from three sources: role (the agent's .md), caller (each consumer listed in agents/registry.json and what it parses), and side_effect (files written, required tool calls). Every check records its source tag and file:line. Checks with no citable source are dropped. Source disagreements are listed for the user to pick a winner. Before approval, grade.py runs the draft over the harvested history. The approval screen shows each check with its source, historical pass rate and 1 or 2 real failing examples. On approval the contract is frozen with a sha256 of every cited file, the historical pass rates are saved as the free baseline, and the queue entry advances to stage cases. A check type the 7 built-ins cannot express is proposed as a new type in the shared grade.py and needs explicit user approval. Custom grading code never goes in an agent folder. The skill has no flags.
acceptance_criteria: Running /improve-agent-benchmarks artifact-grounding-judge produces a draft contract where every check has a source tag and file:line citation
The approval screen shows historical pass rate and real failing examples per check before anything is frozen
The approved contract.json stores a fingerprint hash per cited file and queue.json shows the agent at stage cases

No unit test files (per the no-unit-tests-for-infra rule). Verified by running the contract stage on artifact-grounding-judge end to end and confirming the frozen baseline numbers match a fresh grade.py run
tasks.summary: Added improve-agent-benchmarks SKILL.md and six scripts under scripts/agent-eval/ (bench_lib, bench_queue, contract_sources, contract_review, contract_resolve, contract_freeze). Freeze path verified in scratch dir, baseline matched fresh grade.py on all 7 checks. Opus draft step not run in AFK, draft contract hand-written to exercise scripts. No contract/baseline/queue for the agent committed.

tasks.title: Cases stage: frozen real inputs plus script-verified planted defects
tasks.description: Implement the cases stage for the agent at stage cases. harvest.py selects 4 to 6 recent, varied spawns and freezes them as fixtures under claude-code-shared/evals/<agent>/fixtures/ (gitignored) with a lock file of sha256 hashes. Files a spawn referenced that no longer exist (for example /tmp/seed-*.json) are rebuilt from the parent session log, or that spawn is skipped and the reason logged. For agents that make judgment calls, a Sonnet subagent proposes one find/replace edit per planted case. A script confirms each edit matches exactly once and records the expected verdict in cases.jsonl. Clean cases carry their expected answer too. Import the existing artifact-grounding-judge and persona-accuracy test cases and fixtures once into this format. The queue entry advances to stage iterate.
acceptance_criteria: Running the skill on artifact-grounding-judge at stage cases writes cases.jsonl with real frozen inputs and planted cases, each with an expected answer
A planted edit that matches zero or two-plus times is rejected by the script and never written to cases.jsonl
The existing artifact-grounding-judge and persona-accuracy test cases load in the new format with their expected answers intact
No unit test files (per the no-unit-tests-for-infra rule). Verified by re-hashing fixtures against the lock file and diffing 3 planted cases against their clean base
tasks.summary: Cases stage: cases_lib/import/freeze/plant/finish.py plus SKILL.md section. artifact-grounding-judge has 55 cases (46 imported, 6 real frozen with sha256 lock, 3 planted). Zero-match and multi-match planted edits rejected. Planted edits hand-written, Sonnet proposal step not run in AFK. Legacy cases.jsonl renamed cases.legacy.jsonl for both agents, build_cases.py and run-eval.mjs updated.

tasks.title: Sandboxed live runner with write shims and faked child agents
tasks.description: Build claude-code-shared/scripts/agent-eval/run.mjs from the persona-accuracy run-eval.mjs lessons: claude -p --agent on the agent's production model from resources/model-tiers.json, user hooks and plugins disabled, autoupdater off, a temp working directory and temp learnings file per run, harness errors and usage-limit notices recorded separately from scores. Shims in claude-code-shared/scripts/agent-eval/shims/ replace gh, log-learning.py and external MCP write tools. Each shim records the call and arguments to a shim log and returns canned success. When the agent under test spawns a child agent, a shim returns that child's real recorded output from the same session log. file_written and tool_called checks grade against the shim log. An agent whose external writes cannot be faked safely is marked history-only and gets no live runs. The run writes traces under .claude/agent-bench/<agent>/traces/ (gitignored) and grade.py scores them.
acceptance_criteria: A live baseline run of artifact-grounding-judge cases completes with every log-learning.py call captured in the shim log and nothing appended to the real unified-learnings.jsonl
A run of one attribution-tracer case returns the recorded artifact-grounding-judge output via the child shim with no real child spawn
Harness errors appear in a separate errors file and are excluded from pass rates
No unit test files (per the no-unit-tests-for-infra rule). Verified by diffing unified-learnings.jsonl before and after the live runs (no change) and grading the traces with grade.py
tasks.summary: run.mjs sandboxed runner, shims (log-learning.py, gh, pretool_hook.py faking child agents), child_lookup.py, grade.py reads shim log. Live runs: 6 judge cases (haiku), 1 tracer case (sonnet), about $0.47 total. Real unified-learnings.jsonl byte-identical before and after. Tracer child spawn answered from recorded output.

tasks.title: Iterate stage: one fix, strict keep rule, commit and push to main
tasks.description: Implement one iteration for an agent at stage iterate. Choose the worst failing check from the baseline. A Sonnet analyzer reads only the failing traces and proposes one fix. It must consider a script fix before a prompt edit. Apply the fix, live-run only that check's cases plus a few already-passing sentinels (about 10 to 15 sessions). Keep the fix only if at least half the targeted failing cases now pass, each flip passes again on a second run (2 of 2), no sentinel regresses, and tokens per case stay within 1.5x unless the user approves. Otherwise revert. A kept fix is one commit with message agent-bench(<agent>): <check> fix, pushed straight to main via ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxpush. Only the agent edit, contract.json, the case list and scores are committed. The SHA is recorded in the agent's history. After 2 reverted fixes in a row on the same check, mark it stuck, move to the next failing check, and list both attempts in the report. Then stop. The next iteration is a new invocation.
acceptance_criteria: One invocation on artifact-grounding-judge at stage iterate runs one analyzer call and only the targeted plus sentinel cases
A fix that flips cases but breaks a sentinel is reverted and the working tree is clean afterward
A kept fix lands as a single commit on main via gxpush with the SHA recorded in the agent's history
No unit test files (per the no-unit-tests-for-infra rule). Verified by one real iteration on artifact-grounding-judge and checking the keep/revert decision against the recorded per-case results
tasks.summary: iterate.py, iterate_lib.py, iterate_commit.py plus SKILL.md iterate section. One real iteration on artifact-grounding-judge (no_prose check): fix flipped 1 of 2 targets, failed second confirm, reverted, tree clean. Kept-fix commit path verified with --dry-run only. Live gxpush to main NOT exercised (not approved for AFK run). No frozen contract.json for the agent exists yet.

tasks.title: Start-of-run checks: real-world confirmation, stale contracts, end states
tasks.description: At the start of every invocation for an agent, run three zero-token checks before any stage work. Confirmation: harvest spawns made after each kept fix's commit went live on main and grade them with the history-gradable checks (shape, quote, side effect). Mark the fix confirmed, unconfirmed or regressed. Regressed prints the exact git revert <sha>. Role checks are not confirmable this way and are labeled so. Staleness: compare the stored fingerprint of every cited file. If one changed and the change was not a commit made by this skill, re-run only the checks that cite it, show before/after and historical pass rates, and block live runs until the user approves. End states: an agent whose checks all pass on planted cases and history is passing and drops to the bottom of the queue. It reopens when a cited file changes, a fix regresses, or new production failures raise its failure rate.
acceptance_criteria: After a kept fix and new production spawns exist, the next invocation reports confirmed, unconfirmed or regressed for that fix
Editing a file cited by the contract by hand triggers review of only the checks that cite it, and no live run starts before approval
A commit made by this skill does not trigger a stale-contract review
No unit test files (per the no-unit-tests-for-infra rule). Verified by touching a cited file on a scratch branch and by grading post-fix spawns of artifact-grounding-judge
tasks.summary: preflight.py: fix confirmation (confirmed/unconfirmed/regressed with git revert sha), stale-contract review limited to citing checks, approval gate, end-state flagging. iterate.py refuses to start before approval, rank.py sorts end-state agents last. Verified on scratch branch and scratch dirs over 21 real spawns.

tasks.title: Queue ranking, no-name prompt, and automatic agent onboarding
tasks.description: Rank queue.json entries by historical failure rate times spawn count, with passing agents at the bottom. With no agent name, the first step asks which agent and shows the top 4 with their ranking reason, accepting any typed name. Each invocation checks claude-code-shared/agents/ (recursive) against the queue and adds any missing agent at stage contract with zero history. Update the register-skill skill so registering an agent also adds its queue entry. The skill always runs the next stage for the chosen agent. The user never picks a stage.
acceptance_criteria: Running the skill with no name shows the top 4 agents with failure rate, spawn count and reason
Adding a new agent .md file without /register-skill puts it in the queue on the next invocation
/register-skill on a new agent adds a queue entry at stage contract
No unit test files (per the no-unit-tests-for-infra rule). Verified by running the skill with no argument against the real 34-agent tree and checking the ranking math for 2 agents by hand
tasks.summary: rank.py ranks queue by failure rate x spawns, top 4 prompt, auto-onboards agents from agents/ tree. bench_queue.py sync and ensure commands. register-skill gains step 3d. Ranking math verified by hand for lint-runner and test-runner. Agents tree has 33 .md files, not 34.

tasks.title: Plain-English summary page, CLAUDE.md rule, and skill registration
tasks.description: After each invocation, a script writes a plain-English summary page for the agent under .claude/agent-bench/<agent>/ covering stage done, checks flipped, kept or reverted, commit SHA, confirmation status and any stuck checks. It is fully separate from hillclimb and eval-report.sh. Add a CLAUDE.md line saying agent-bench results get their plain-English summary from this script. Register the new skill via the register-skill chain (model-tiers.json skills map at Sonnet tier, registry entries) and add the shared learning-capture tail.
acceptance_criteria: Every invocation writes the summary page and prints its path
The global CLAUDE.md report rule mentions agent-bench and its summary script
improve-agent-benchmarks appears in model-tiers.json and passes the register-skill verification steps
No unit test files (per the no-unit-tests-for-infra rule). Verified by opening the summary page after a real artifact-grounding-judge iteration and checking its numbers against the scores file
tasks.summary: summary.py writes .claude/agent-bench/<agent>/summary.html. CLAUDE.md rule added (global file symlinks to repo .claude/CLAUDE.md). Skill registered in model-tiers.json at T3. Page verified on synthetic data only, no real iteration scores exist.
